summary: Independent read-only review of the player redesign, three rounds, by a reviewer separate from the implementer, comparing old and new VideoPlayer.tsx block by block. Reviewed on a working branch that also carried other unfinished screens; the five player commits are applied here on their own, and every player-owned file was checked byte-identical to the reviewed state, with the shared stylesheet differing only in card, rail and title-page rules. Round 1 was FIX-FIRST: a new transport Next-episode button let a party host mark an episode watched from any position and move the room through a control that looked like the solo one (now not offered to anyone in a party; party advancement is the Up next card as before); plus Resync hidden on narrow phones, focus lost when sheets close, arrow keys falling through to player shortcuts, and party chrome overlapping the new controls. Round 2 was FIX-FIRST for one regression the fixes introduced: in a party with the room connected the bars never auto-hid (a per-render callback re-armed the hide timer). Round 3: lows-only. Throughout, the reviewer found delivery choice, session start and recovery, casting, party sync, subtitle holds and progress saving textually untouched, seeks, picks, speed and picture in picture going through the existing paths, the surface contract with the app unchanged, and no pre-existing test assertion weakened. Remaining lows: the reaction picker is not closed on minimise; a menu open when a fatal error arrives stays open with nothing drawn; 'Tap for sound' may meet the Skip button at 640 to 720px with the party rail open; three small behaviours untested; nits. Not verifiable here and listed in the pull request: real Safari and iPhone, Android, Chromecast, AirPlay, touch gestures, a real multi-person party with voice, screen readers. Reviewer ran only the contrast calculator; Go suite, tsc, 1823 unit tests and the full audit were run green on this commit.
